# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.
# New marketing site (`/nxm`, staging only) — how pages are built and wired

The new site is the design package's own pages (`/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff`) ported by generators, with the owner's identity picks applied and **every price, plan, game, mod, post and region read from the system at request time**. Owner's rules: nothing hardcoded; SEO on every page (incl. dynamic ones); portal never touched; no production deploy until the whole site is ready; staging only (`app/nxm/layout.tsx` 404s outside `NXEON_ENV=staging`).

## Generators (never hand-edit their outputs)
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_home.py` → homepage (`app/nxm/page.tsx` + `_home/*`, `home.css`).
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py [slug ...]` → every inner page: runs the package's own builders, captures the page, then writes `app/nxm/_pages/<slug>/{page.css,content.ts,script.ts}` and the route file(s) `app/nxm/<route>/page.tsx`. Ends with a **real-data audit**: every page must say `wired` with no `stale` values before launch.
- Shared transforms: `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py` (routes, link mapping, CSS scoping, buttons, review/nav slots).

## Wiring a page to real data
1. **`tools/nxm/wire/<slug_with_underscores>.py`** — rewrites the design's snapshot data in the generated page:
   - `def body(html) -> html`: replace snapshot markup/values with slots `{{nxm:key}}` (escaped text) or `{{nxm:key:html}}` (trusted server-rendered markup).
   - `def js(src) -> src`: replace snapshot constants with values from `__NXM` (the page's data), e.g. `const(src, "VPS", "__NXM.vps")`. `__NXM` is parsed from `<script id="nxm-data">` before the page script runs.
   - `ALLOW = {...}`: `$`-amounts on the page that are NOT our prices (competitor prices with a source, a "$0.00 spent" illustration).
   - Use `_w.py` helpers (`sub`, `resub`, `const`): they assert the target exists, so a design change can never silently leave a snapshot value.
2. **`app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts`** — the loader, server-only:
   - `export async function load(p: Record<string,string>): Promise<NxmLoad>` → `{ slots, data, jsonLd, crumb }`.
   - `export async function meta(p): Promise<Partial<SeoEntry> & {image?, type?}>` — REQUIRED for template routes (title/description from the item: mod name, post title…); optional for static pages whose SEO depends on live data.
   - Read data through the system's own modules (see below) — the same tables/helpers checkout and the live site use. Throw when required data is missing (fail closed); never fall back to a snapshot.
   - Deploy/buy links: `deployHref()` from `lib/deploy-intent.ts` with real ids (plan id, game family + tier id, region).
   - Shared helpers: `app/nxm/_data/lib.ts` (vpsPlans, vpsTermMap, gameTiers, gameName, liveRegions, usd, esc, introSpan, productLd, NxmLoad) and `cards.ts` (plan card renderers). Page-group helpers go in your own `_data/<group>-*.ts` file.
3. Re-run `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py <slug>` and check the audit line.

## Template routes (catalogues)
- A route with `[params]` in `ROUTES` (nxmlib) is served for every item; the loader gets `p` (e.g. `{family, slug}`) and must 404 unknown items (`notFound()` from `next/navigation`).
- A page fanned out to many fixed routes (e.g. one game template → `/rust-server-hosting`, …) is listed in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`: `[{"route": "/rust-server-hosting", "params": {"family": "rust"}}]`.

## SEO (every page)
- `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`: title/description/breadcrumb per production route (seeded from the live site's rendered metadata). Dynamic pages provide theirs via `meta()`.
- `nxmMetadata()` adds canonical (production route), OG/Twitter, noindex until launch.
- `NxmPage` emits BreadcrumbList (from the route), FAQPage (parsed from the page's own `<details><summary>` FAQ) and whatever `jsonLd` the loader returns (Product/AggregateOffer from real plans via `productLd`, BlogPosting, SoftwareApplication…). Match or exceed the live page's structured data (the live types per route are in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md → "New marketing site").

## Real data sources (use these, not copies)
- VPS: `db.plan` (active, sortOrder) + `lib/intro-pricing.ts` + `lib/billing-terms.ts` (`VPS_TERMS`, `termDiscountPct`) + `lib/annual-discount.ts`; disk add-on `lib/disk-expand.ts extraDiskPerGbCents()`; dedicated IPv4 `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`.
- Web hosting `db.hostingPlan`; email `db.emailPlan` (per-month = price/termMonths); NxCloud `db.nxCloudPlan`; the pricing explorer's combined view `lib/pricing-explorer-data.ts getPricingExplorerData()`.
- Domains: `POPULAR_TLDS` in `components/marketing/tlds.ts` ("from" prices; live search uses the registrar).
- Games: `lib/games.ts` (`GAME_FAMILIES`, `GAME_DISPLAY`, `GAME_ART_SLUG` → `public/games/art/*`, `GAME_GENRES`), tiers `db.gamePlan` (per family, per-month = price/termMonths), regions = enabled `db.node` rows + `lib/node-regions.ts` labels.
- Mods: `lib/mods-catalog.ts` (`queryCatalogMods`, `listCatalogFamilies`, `listFeaturedMods`, `listTopDownloadedMods`, `listRecentlyUpdatedMods`, `getCatalogMod`, `relatedCatalogMods`, …) — public = `active && upstreamOk`.
- Blog: `lib/blog.ts` (`getPublishedPosts`, `getPostsPage`, `getPublishedPost`, `renderArticle`, `getRelatedPosts`, `productLinkForPost`). Hide the internal `seobatch` tag from public tag lists.
- Contact: server action `submitContact` in `lib/actions-contact.ts` (categories `lib/contact-categories.ts`); newsletter `subscribe` in `lib/actions-newsletter.ts`.
- Status: `lib/monitoring.ts` + `lib/status-copy.ts`. Reviews: `app/nxm/_components/ReviewBadges.tsx` (real only).

## Verify
- Dev server on 3033 (shared): `curl http://localhost:3033/nxm<route>`; the port's audit; `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (ignore `.next/types` noise); screenshots vs `dist/nxeon-<slug>.html` at 1440 and 390.

## Native pages (pages the design package doesn't include)
- Author in the package's own format under `tools/nxm/native/<slug>/`: `body.html` (with `{{SPRITE}}`, `{{NAV}}`, `{{FOOTER}}`), `page.css`, `page.js`, `meta.json` (`title`, `description`, `anchors`, `assets`). `port_pages.py` assembles them exactly like the package's `build_page.py` (shared shell + common.css + Aurora + your css/js) and runs the same pipeline. Add the slug to `ROUTES` in `nxmlib.py` (or a fan-out in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`).
- Free tools: `native/tools` (hub) and `native/tools-app` (every tool page, routes/tools-app.json); `native/tools-tool` is the original template, kept unchanged for the skin creator only. See docs/DOCUMENTATION.md → "Free tools overhaul".
- Reference implementations: `native/about` (story + liquid-glass photo + real product prices), `native/security` (diagram + card grids + the Compare page's disclosure board), `native/affiliate` (data-driven promo), `native/legal` (article reading layout, 4 routes from one template).
- Write markup with the DESIGN's classes (`au-btn`, `au-btn--glass`, `au-card`, `au-glass`, `h2pill`, `gp-head`, `h2`, `lede`, `section`, `container`, `faq-wrap`/`faq`, `wh-final`, `data-au-icon="…" data-grad`) — the porter maps buttons to the library hierarchy. Links to other pages as `https://nxeon.cloud/<route>` (the porter makes them relative / keeps ported ones inside /nxm).
- Pure-copy pages: a wire module with `STATIC = True` and no loader.
- Body attributes: `<body class="pg-x" style="--acc:…" data-…>` land on the page wrapper; `.pg-x …` selectors are rewritten to match it.
- Loader extras: `trail` (breadcrumb below Home when ancestors aren't in the registry), `particles` (per-item colours), `crumb`.
- Interactive React pieces (e.g. a live tool component) can be mounted into a slot element with a small client component + `createPortal` — see `app/nxm/_components/HeroParticles.tsx`.
- SEO for new routes: add an entry to `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts` (title/description/crumb) or return them from `meta(p)`.
- The box is also production: keep Playwright runs sequential (one browser at a time) and don't restart the shared dev server (:3033, 4 GB heap cap).

content.thinking:
I'm realizing seed mods on template games shouldn't appear as real mods in a marketing demo — I should only show categories plus a clearly-labeled demo "forged" mod, with everything else just showing "Forge new". I'm planning a React component, CyrusDemo, mounted via createPortal similar to the existing HeroParticles/ToolMount pattern, to render this demo state.

I'm sketching a lightweight 2D canvas network view using buildGraph from graph.ts for games without seed mods, with curved links, rounded game logos, and category icons, layered over a single shared WebGL context (createCoreGL/createCoreDriver + fx bus) that lazy-starts via IntersectionObserver, pauses offscreen, and falls back to a static frame for reduced motion. I'm scripting a typed prompt ("Make me a Minecraft mod where...") that triggers a routing animation — highlighting the Minecraft branch, then Weapons category, packets traveling the path, and a demo mod pill ("Frostbite Greatsword (demo)") appearing alongside a side card showing the CYRUS_STAGES pipeline and a short code snippet, all clearly labeled as a demo.

I'm also adding 3-4 scripted prompt chips that route to different games — one live Minecraft weapon flow, one Minecraft economy/quest flow, and a Valheim chip that honestly surfaces a "coming soon, template preview" message since non-Minecraft games in the studio only produce template previews rather than live compiles. I'm considering letting users type a free-text prompt that gets routed through a simple client-side classifier using GAMES aliases and CATEGORIES keywords, which would be a real (if limited) slice of the actual routing logic.

The demo would then "forge" a result showing the routed game, category, recommended model, complexity, detected features, and a token estimate pulled from the real reserve table and estimate() function — genuine logic wrapped in a scripted forging animation, which feels honest: "type a mod idea, see where Cyrus routes it and what it would cost."

For the hero section, I'm sketching motion ideas around the coin (tilt/parallax with a specular sheen) and considering an SVG line-draw animation tracing the Y-mark's sweep and arm paths in gradient strokes behind the coin as a calm, restrained visual flourish.

Refining that further: a slowly rotating coin responding to pointer movement with damping, paired with a light sweep using the coin image itself as a CSS mask so a moving gradient highlight glides across its surface — like a minted coin catching light. Beneath it, I'm picturing thin hairline curves radiating from the coin out to six small game logos, echoing a network/mind-map structure rooted at the core, drawn in once via stroke animation rather than looping indefinitely.

Now I need to check whether the NXM marketing site actually supports a light theme, since everything customer-facing is supposed to work in both dark and light modes — I should look at nxm.css for a data-theme attribute.

content.content:
// `nx-has-banner` publishes the sandbox banner's height as --nx-chrome.
    // Full-height "app frame" routes (the mail client) size themselves to the
    // viewport minus the fixed chrome above them, and this banner is real
    // chrome here that does not exist in production — without it the mail page
    // would be exactly one banner too tall and scroll in the sandbox only.
    <html lang="en" className={`${nxSans.variable} ${nxMono.variable}`} suppressHydrationWarning>
      <head>
        {/* Applies the saved theme BEFORE first paint. A React effect runs after
            hydration, which is one paint too late — every load would flash the
            dark theme at anyone who chose light. Deliberately tiny, deliberately
            blocking, and it fails closed to dark.

            Gated to /dashboard: `nx-theme` lives in localStorage, which is
            shared by the WHOLE origin, not just the portal — the toggle only
            renders inside the dashboard shell, but without this check, a

# ── native pages: pages the design package doesn't include ─────────────────
# Authored in the package's own page format (body.html with {{SPRITE}}/{{NAV}}/
# {{FOOTER}}, page.css, page.js, meta.json) under tools/nxm/native/<slug>/ and
# assembled exactly like the package's build_page.py: shared shell + common.css
# + aurora + the page's own css/js. Then the same pipeline as every page.
NATIVE = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/native"
def build_native(slug):
    D = f"{NATIVE}/{slug}/"
    meta = json.load(open(D + "meta.json"))
    p1, p2, p3 = (open(f"{SRC}/part{i}.html").read() for i in (1, 2, 3))
    MAIN = "https://claude.ai/artifact/KryegJ1sG3zYzX7MyxypYs"
    head = re.sub(r"<title>.*?</title>", f"<title>{meta['title']}</title>", p1, count=1)
    head = re.sub(r'<meta name="description" content="[^"]*">', f'<meta name="description" content="{meta["description"]}">', head, count=1)
    head = head.replace('url("__IMG_HERO2__")', "none").replace('url("__IMG_GRAIN__")', "none")
    css = open(f"{SRC}/pages/common.css").read() + AURORA_CSS + (open(D + "page.css").read() if os.path.exists(D + "page.css") else "")
    head = head.replace("</style>", css + "</style>", 1)
    sprite = p2[p2.index("<body>") + 6:p2.index("</svg>") + 6]
    local = set(meta.get("anchors", []))
    def fix_links(h):
        h = re.sub(r'href="#([a-z-]*)"', lambda m: f'href="#{m.group(1)}"' if (m.group(1) in local or m.group(1).startswith("i-")) else f'href="{MAIN}#{m.group(1)}"', h)
        return h.replace(f'href="{MAIN}#top"', f'href="{MAIN}"')
    nav = fix_links(p2[p2.index('<a class="skip"'):p2.index("</header>") + 9]).replace(f'href="{MAIN}#main"', 'href="#main"')
    nav = nav.replace('<a class="logo" href="#top"', f'<a class="logo" href="{MAIN}"')
    footer = fix_links(p2[p2.index('<footer class="footer"'):p2.index("</footer>") + 9])
    body = open(D + "body.html").read()
    for k, v in {"SPRITE": sprite, "NAV": nav, "FOOTER": footer, "MAIN": MAIN}.items():
        body = body.replace("{{" + k + "}}", v)
    helpers = p3[p3.index("<script>"):p3.index("/* ------------------------------------------------------------------")]
    def blk(a, b): i = p3.index(a); j = p3.index(b, i + len(a)); return p3[i:j]
    js = helpers + "document.getElementById('year') && (document.getElementById('year').textContent = new Date().getFullYear());\n"
    js += blk("/* ============ Navigation ============ */", "/* ============ Reveal, rules")
    js += blk("/* ============ Reveal, rules, in-view hooks, counters ============ */", "/* ============ Hero: Power Your")
    js += AURORA_JS + "\n" + (open(D + "page.js").read() if os.path.exists(D + "page.js") else "") + "\n})();\n</script>\n</body>\n</html>\n"
    html = head + body + js
    A = f"{PKG}/assets/"
    m = {k: (v if v.startswith("/") else A + v) for k, v in meta.get("assets", {}).items()}
    m.setdefault("LOGO", A + "logo.png")
    for _k in ["minecraft", "rust", "palworld", "valheim", "ark", "cs2"]:
        m.setdefault("NAV_" + _k.upper(), A + "nav/" + _k + ".webp")
    mime = lambda q: "image/png" if q.endswith(".png") else "image/svg+xml" if q.endswith(".svg") else "image/jpeg" if q.endswith(".jpg") else "image/webp"
    for k in sorted(m, key=len, reverse=True):
        html = html.replace(f"__IMG_{k}__", f"data:{mime(m[k])};base64," + _fake_b64(open(m[k], "rb").read()).decode())
    left = set(re.findall(r"__IMG_[A-Za-z0-9_]+__", html)); assert not left, left
    return html

EXT = {"image/png": "png", "image/webp": "webp", "image/jpeg": "jpg", "image/svg+xml": "svg", "image/gif": "gif"}
def externalise(s):
    def rep(m):
        h = m.group(2); ext = EXT.get(m.group(1), "bin")
        path = f"{ASSET_DIR}/{h}.{ext}"
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            open(path, "wb").write(_blobs[h])
        return f"/nxm/a/{h}.{ext}"
    s = re.sub(r"data:([\w/+.-]+);base64,NXMA([0-9a-f]{16})", rep, s)
    assert "NXMA" not in s
    return s

AURORA_CSS = open(f"{SRC}/pages/aurora.css").read()
AURORA_JS = open(f"{SRC}/pages/aurora.built.js").read()

def port(slug):
    html = externalise(build_native(slug) if os.path.isdir(f"{NATIVE}/{slug}") else build(slug))
    head, rest = html.split("</head>", 1)
    title = re.search(r"<title>(.*?)</title>", head).group(1)
    desc_m = re.search(r'<meta name="description" content="([^"]*)"', head)
    desc = desc_m.group(1) if desc_m else ""

    # CSS: the page's one stylesheet minus Aurora (already loaded, scoped, by
    # app/nxm/layout.tsx), scoped under this page's wrapper.
    css = re.search(r"<style>([\s\S]*)</style>", head).group(1)
    assert AURORA_CSS in css, "aurora.css not found verbatim"
    css = geist(css.replace(AURORA_CSS, ""))
    scope, rootcls = f".nxm-p-{slug}", f":root.nxm-p-{slug}-root"
    # the design's <body …>: its classes, CSS variables and data-* move to the
    # page wrapper (a nested page can't touch <body>); `xray` is a class the
    # design's JS toggles on body
    btag = re.search(r"<body([^>]*)>", html).group(1)
    battr = lambda n: (re.search(rf'{n}="([^"]*)"', btag) or [None, ""])[1]
    bclasses = battr("class").split()
    body_attrs = {"cls": " ".join(bclasses), "style": battr("style"),
                  "data": {k: v for k, v in re.findall(r'data-([\w-]+)="([^"]*)"', btag)}}
    hoisted, rules = scope_css(css, scope, rootcls, frozenset(bclasses) | {"xray"})
    extra = (f"\n{scope}{{{FONT_VARS}}}\n"
             f"{rootcls}{{--nav-h:68px;background:#060913}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta:only-child{{grid-column:1/-1}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nxm-navcta{{white-space:nowrap}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta{{height:48px;justify-content:center;font-size:1rem}}\n"
             f"@media (max-width:1080px){{{scope} .nv-act>.nxm-navcta{{display:none}}}}\n")
    css_out = ("/* GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py from the design package — do not edit. */\n"
               + "\n".join(hoisted) + "\n" + "\n".join(rules) + extra)

    # Markup: everything between <body> and the page script.
    js_at = rest.rfind("<script>")
    body, js = rest[:js_at], rest[js_at:]
    body = re.sub(r"^\s*<body[^>]*>", "", body.strip())
    body = relink(body)
    for old, new in FIXES.get(slug, []):
        assert old in body, (slug, old); body = body.replace(old, new)
    body, btns = swap_buttons(body)
    body, nrev = reviews_slot(body)
    body, ncta, nlogin, npost = nav_slots(body)
    assert ncta == 2 and nlogin == 2 and npost == 1, (slug, ncta, nlogin, npost)
    body, nfoot = re.subn(r'<footer class="footer"[\s\S]*?</footer>', "", body)
    assert nfoot == 1, (slug, nfoot)
    body = re.sub(r"<!--(?!NXM:)[\s\S]*?-->", "", body)
    stray = balanced(body)
    assert not stray, f"{slug}: stray end tags {stray[:3]}"
    wire = load_wire(slug)
    if wire and hasattr(wire, "body"):
        body = wire.body(body)

    # Script: the page's JS minus the Aurora runtime (mounted once by the layout).
    js = re.search(r"<script>([\s\S]*)</script>", js).group(1)
    assert AURORA_JS in js, "aurora.built.js not found verbatim"
    js = js.replace(AURORA_JS, "")
    js = js.replace("https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js", "/nxm/three.min.js")
    # body attributes now live on the page wrapper
    js = js.replace("document.body.dataset", "document.querySelector('.nxm-p').dataset")
    js = js.replace("document.body.classList.toggle('xray'", "document.querySelector('.nxm-p').classList.toggle('xray'")
    js = relink(js)
    for old, new in FIXES.get(slug, []):
        js = js.replace(old, new)
    js = js_buttons(js)
    if wire and hasattr(wire, "js"):
        js = "var __NXM = JSON.parse((document.getElementById('nxm-data') || {}).textContent || 'null');\n" + wire.js(js)
    # Money in the visitor's display currency (NxmPage emits #nxm-fx): the same
    # rules as the live site's convertAndFormat; USD keeps the design's "$12.99".
    js = js.replace("'$' + Math.round(v).toLocaleString('en-US')", "__nxmMoney(Math.round(v), 0)")
    js = re.sub(r"'\$' \+ v\.toLocaleString\('en-US'(?:, \{[^}]*\})?\)", "__nxmMoney(v)", js)
    js = js.replace("'$' + v.toFixed(2)", "__nxmMoney(v)")
    assert "'$' +" not in js, f"{slug}: unconverted '$' + … money formatting in the page script"
    js = FX_PRELUDE + js
    assert "cdnjs" not in js and "claude.ai/artifact" not in js and "claude.ai/artifact" not in body
    stale = audit(slug, body, js, getattr(wire, "ALLOW", set()) if wire else set())
    STATUS[slug] = ("static (no system data)" if (wire is not None and getattr(wire, "STATIC", False)) else "wired" if wire else "NOT WIRED") + (f", stale {stale}" if stale else "")

    d = f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages/{slug}"; os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    open(f"{d}/page.css", "w").write(css_out)
    open(f"{d}/content.ts", "w").write(
        "// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit. Trusted, static markup\n"
        "// from the owner's own design package (never user input).\n"
        f"export const TITLE = {json.dumps(title)};\n"
        f"export const DESCRIPTION = {json.dumps(desc)};\n"
        f"export const BODY_HTML = {json.dumps(body)};\n"
        f"export const BODY_ATTRS = {json.dumps(body_attrs)};\n")
    open(f"{d}/script.ts", "w").write(
        "// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit. The page's own script.\n"
        f"export const PAGE_SCRIPT = {json.dumps(js)};\n")

    route = ROUTES[slug]
    loader = wire is not None and os.path.exists(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts")
    static = bool(wire is not None and getattr(wire, "STATIC", False))
    assert wire is None or loader or static, f"{slug}: wire module without app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts"
    has_meta = loader and "export async function meta" in open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts").read()
    for r, fixed in routes_for(slug):
        if ("[" in r or fixed) and not has_meta:
            STATUS[slug] = STATUS.get(slug, "") + f" (route {r} not written: template needs its loader)"
            continue
        write_route(slug, r, fixed, loader)
    print(f"{slug:36} {BASE}{route if route != '/' else ''}  css {len(css_out)//1024}KB  body {len(body)//1024}KB  "
          f"js {len(js)//1024}KB  buttons {btns}  reviews {nrev}")
    return slug

# ── routes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A page is a TEMPLATE when its route has [params] (e.g. /mods/[family]/[slug])
# or when tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json fans it out to many fixed routes
# (e.g. the game template -> /rust-server-hosting {family: "rust"}, ...).
# Loaders get the params: load(p) / meta(p).
def routes_for(slug):
    f = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/routes/{slug}.json"
    if os.path.exists(f):
        return [(e["route"], e.get("params", {})) for e in json.load(open(f))]
    return [(ROUTES[slug], {})]

def write_route(slug, route, fixed, loader):
    """One route file. Every route passes its [params], fixed template params
    and ?query (search, pagination, ?topic= deep links…) into the loader as one
    map; the concrete path (/mods/[family]/[slug] -> /mods/minecraft/lithium)
    is used for canonical and breadcrumbs."""
    rd = f"{ROOT}/app/nxm{route}"; os.makedirs(rd, exist_ok=True)
    rel = os.path.relpath(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm", rd)
    pc = PARTICLES.get(slug)
    particles = f' particles={{{{ from: "{pc[0]}", to: "{pc[1]}" }}}}' if pc else ""
    # loader-supplied colours (e.g. per game) win over the slug default
    pdefault = f' ?? {{ from: "{pc[0]}", to: "{pc[1]}" }}' if pc else ""
    has_meta = loader and "export async function meta" in open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts").read()
    dyn = "[" in route
    assert not (dyn or fixed) or has_meta, f"{slug}: template routes need a loader with meta(p) for SEO"
    path_expr = ("`" + re.sub(r"\[(\w+)\]", r"${p.\1}", route) + "`") if dyn else json.dumps(route)
    if loader:
        imp = (f'import {{ load{", meta" if has_meta else ""} }} from "{rel}/_data/{slug}";\n'
               f'import type {{ NxmLoad }} from "{rel}/_data/lib";\n'
               f'import {{ nxmParams }} from "{rel}/_data/params";\n')
        ptype = "{ params: Promise<Record<string, string>>; searchParams: Promise<Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>> }"
        getp = f"const p = await nxmParams(params, searchParams, {json.dumps(fixed)});"
        metacall = f"nxmMetadata({path_expr}, await meta(p))" if has_meta else f"nxmMetadata({path_expr})"
        body = f"""export async function generateMetadata({{ params, searchParams }}: {ptype}): Promise<Metadata> {{
  {getp}
  return {metacall};
}}

export default async function Page({{ params, searchParams }}: {ptype}) {{
  {getp}
  const d: NxmLoad = await load(p);
  return <NxmPage slug="{slug}" route={{{path_expr}}} body={{C.BODY_HTML}} attrs={{C.BODY_ATTRS}} particles={{d.particles{pdefault}}} slots={{d.slots}} data={{d.data}} jsonLd={{d.jsonLd}} crumb={{d.crumb}} trail={{d.trail}} />;
}}"""
    else:
        imp = ""
        body = f"""export async function generateMetadata(): Promise<Metadata> {{
  return nxmMetadata({path_expr});
}}

export default async function Page() {{
  return <NxmPage slug="{slug}" route={{{path_expr}}} body={{C.BODY_HTML}} attrs={{C.BODY_ATTRS}}{particles} />;
}}"""
    open(f"{rd}/page.tsx", "w").write(f"""// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit.
import type {{ Metadata }} from "next";
import {{ NxmPage }} from "{rel}/_components/NxmPage";
import {{ nxmMetadata }} from "{rel}/_seo/meta";
import * as C from "{rel}/_pages/{slug}/content";
{imp}import "{rel}/_pages/{slug}/page.css";

export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
{body}
""")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    slugs = sys.argv[1:] or [s for s in ROUTES if s != "home"]
    for s in slugs:
        port(s)
    # the client runtime imports each page's script by slug
    keys = sorted(os.listdir(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages"))
    open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages/scripts.ts", "w").write(
        "// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit.\n"
        "// Each page's script is its own chunk, loaded only on that page.\n"
        "export const SCRIPTS: Record<string, () => Promise<{ PAGE_SCRIPT: string }>> = {\n"
        + "".join(f'  {json.dumps(k)}: () => import("./{k}/script"),\n' for k in keys if os.path.isdir(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages/{k}"))
        + "};\n")
    print("\nreal-data audit (launch needs every page 'wired' with no stale prices):")
    for k, v in STATUS.items():
        print(f"  {k:36} {v}")
    print("assets:", len(os.listdir(ASSET_DIR)), "files,",
          sum(os.path.getsize(f"{ASSET_DIR}/{f}") for f in os.listdir(ASSET_DIR)) // 1024 // 1024, "MB")

2. **Templated/boring layout.** Every version was the same skeleton: dark bg + a canvas particle animation + centered eyebrow → stacked sections → stat strip → product grid → pricing → CTA. That IS the "AI slop" they said they don't want. They want bolder, asymmetric, editorial composition.

**How to apply:** build marketing pages ON the existing brand tokens and component primitives, not a new palette. Live homepage is `app/page.tsx`. **2026-08-02 VIDEO BRIEF (board "Website Overhaul" card, 4:51 narrated screen-rec — the authoritative direction).** The user compared THREE sources and wants them combined into a NEW preview version (built `/v8`): (1) a rocket.new AI prototype "Deploy anywhere. name: nxeon-redesign-generic-drift
description: Redesign/mockup-matching work goes generic unless working from the literal reference file with real iterative screenshot comparison
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc
  modified: 2026-08-26T18:58:07.153Z
---

When asked to redesign something to match a provided mockup, the output repeatedly came back "generic" / "nothing like what you generated" — burning the user's tokens on rejected rounds (Singapore hero v4, v5, and the first pass at the network map before it was scoped down and redone carefully).

**Root cause, confirmed by comparing the failures to the one clean success:** the generic outcomes all happened when working from a *description* of the mockup (my own recollection, a text summary, or a mismatched/wrong screenshot) instead of the actual image file. The one case that converged well — [[nxeon-figma-design-system]]'s standalone `SingaporeNetworkMap` component — worked because the agent `Read` the real reference image directly and ran an honest build → screenshot → compare-side-by-side → adjust loop for 4 full rounds before stopping.

**Why:** without a literal image to check against, generation defaults toward the same handful of generic AI-design patterns (the artifact-design skill documents this same failure mode for artifacts). A description, even a careful one written by re-reading the image, loses the specific proportions/positions/details that make a design read as "this one" instead of "a plausible one."

**How to apply, every time a redesign/mockup match is requested:**
1. Get the literal reference file onto disk (ask the user to paste it to wherever's convenient — this session used the Nxeon admin board — rather than working from a text description of it, even a detailed one).
2. Do NOT stop after one build pass. Screenshot the actual result, `Read` it next to the reference, and explicitly check composition, spacing, colors, and copy before calling it done. Iterate at least 2-3 rounds as a default, more if it's still off.
3. When the user says "stop relying on our existing site styling, make it look different" — that instruction itself is a signal the generic-drift risk is high; take it as seriously as a literal image mismatch.
4. If dispatching a subagent for the actual build, hand it the reference file path directly and put the same iterate-and-compare loop in its instructions explicitly — don't assume it will do this on its own.

**2026-10-07 Bare Metal concepts:** round 1 (standalone static HTML mockups, flat cards, no owner art) was rejected outright: "not a good representation of the current visual language… assets and styling just isn't the same", "portal ones too basic", "tags should be actual tags". # Brief: studio-ui: the Cyrus studio fixes

Read `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/CONTEXT.md` first (the owner's full request, the shared rules, the roster). Worktree: `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-studio -b feature/cyrus-v6-studio feature/cyrus-v6`. Output dir for notes: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/studio/`.

## Your scope (UI fixes, brand and plans)
Do all of these, in the existing v5 code (`components/cyrus/`, `app/dashboard/cyrus/`, `components/cyrus-tokens/`, nav in `app/dashboard/layout.tsx` + `lib/nx/*`):
1. **Remove "choose the heart of Cyrus".** Delete the core gallery route `/dashboard/cyrus/cores`, the "Cores" button in the top bar, "Use this core", the command-palette entry and any core-selection state. Particle Nebula is THE core. Remove the unused core concepts from the bundle (`components/cyrus/cosmos/cores/concepts/*` other than particles) and the gallery components, so the page ships less JS. Keep the core renderer itself unchanged (pixel-identical).
2. **Remove the "Hierarchy" legend** in the bottom-left of the network.
3. **Add game limited to games Cyrus actually supports** (the six in `lib/cyrus/games.ts` and anything with a `lib/cyrus/games/<id>.ts` support file). No free-text custom games. If every supported game is already on the ring, hide the dashed "Add game" branch/button rather than showing a dead end; otherwise the dialog lists only supported games not yet on the ring, each with its status (Live / Coming soon) and loader. Tell me what you decided.
4. **Expandable side preview card**: a clear expand/collapse control (and keyboard shortcut + Esc to collapse) that widens the preview panel to most of the stage (code gets room), remembered per browser, works at 390 px (full-screen sheet).
5. **Explain tab** alongside Code, Files, Versions, Notes (v4b had one: `git show feature/cyrus-v5~2:components/cyrus/Explain.tsx` and the v4 data `MbCommand/MbPermission/MbConfig/MbFinding` in `lib/modbuilder/types.ts`). Plain-English explanation of what the mod does, its commands, permissions, config options and safety scan result, for real builds; for template games a short generated explanation labelled as a preview.
6. **Model picker legibility**: the picker card from the prompt box is translucent and unreadable. Make it an opaque, high-contrast surface in dark and light (use `--cy-*` tokens; keep the glass feel only on the border/shine), with clear selected state, price/typical-cost line and lock states.
7. **Higher-quality model icons** for **Katara, Saka, Yakko** (original names, see CONTEXT.md). Design three distinct, premium SVG glyphs (a tier language, e.g. one/two/three element growth, consistent stroke weight, gradient version + mono `currentColor` version). Export as React components in `components/cyrus/icons/ModelGlyphs.tsx` (props: size, variant `gradient|mono`) AND standalone SVGs in `public/cyrus/models/{katara,saka,yakko}.svg`. Use them in: the model picker, the token plans card (`components/cyrus-tokens/`), the prompt dock and the token chip tooltip. The marketing agent will import the same files.
8. **Plan estimates** on the token plans cards: "how many edits or mods you can make with this". Compute from the REAL cost table (`lib/cyrus/estimate.ts`, `lib/cyrus/tokens/*`; do not hardcode numbers that can drift), per model and per size (small mod, typical mod, edit/refine), shown as ranges ("about 20 to 35 small mods or 80 to 120 edits on Katara") with an honest "estimate, depends on size" note. Add unit tests for the estimator.
9. **Sidebar nav item for Cyrus**: highlighted treatment (accent glow/underline, kept subtle and premium, works in light mode), and replace the star icon with a **proper SVG Y icon** drawn from the Y mark's shape (see `components/cyrus/icons/cyrusMark.ts` and the white wordmark Y), `currentColor`-driven so it recolours with the nav state and theme. Add it to the portal icon set (`lib/nx/icon-paths.ts`) so `<Icon name="cyrus">` works everywhere; also use it in the command palette and any Cyrus link elsewhere in the portal.
10. **Rounded game logos everywhere**: the Rust logo is a sharp square inside its branch orb. Every game logo (branch orbs, add-game dialog, preview header, chips, token UI) must be clipped to a rounded shape (circle in orbs, rounded-square elsewhere) with `object-fit: cover`/contain as appropriate and a thin ring, so none show hard corners. Check all six at 1x and 2x.
11. **Wire the owner's brand assets** (`docs/cyrus/asset-picks.json`): top-bar mark (Y/wordmark by theme), app icon and favicon (black tile pick; also `app/icon` for the Cyrus pages if the portal allows a per-route icon, else leave), token coin in the chip and plans cards, the neon loading-coin spin set (face, three-quarter, edge) in the thinking/forging states (CSS crossfade like the picker page's, reduced-motion safe), avatar for Cyrus replies (UNDECIDED: use `iconset-r2-1` behind one constant `CYRUS_AVATAR_ASSET` so it is a one-line change). Also build `components/cyrus/brand/BuiltWithCyrusBadge.tsx` with variants `generic | tested | compact` x `dark | light` (auto by theme) from the badge assets; the community agent and marketing agent will use it. Copy needed assets to `public/cyrus/brand/` as webp (keep sizes sensible).
12. **Audit v4b -> v5 regressions**: list features the pre-redesign Cyrus (`feature/cyrus-v5~2`) had that v5 lacks (Explain, source viewer, anything from `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v4/`) and restore the ones not owned by another agent (community/NxLabs, lifecycle, routing, categories are others'). Put the list in your report.

## Verify
Real route `/dashboard/cyrus` on node-2 (see CONTEXT rule 8), dark + light, 1440 + 390; screenshots of every item; `devhost tsc` clean; update/extend `test/cyrus.test.ts`; `gen-light-literals` regenerated if needed (run on node-2, pull the file back).
# Brief: routing: broad prompts, universal categories, listing dialog

Read `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/CONTEXT.md` first (the owner's full request, the shared rules, the roster). Worktree: `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-routing -b feature/cyrus-v6-routing feature/cyrus-v6`. Output dir for notes: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/routing/`.

## Your scope
**A. Broad-request prompt routing.** Today the dock needs a hovered game or mod. Make it understand free requests from anywhere (the core, a game, a mod, or nothing selected): "make me a mod for Minecraft where creepers drop diamonds", "work on my frost axe mod and fix the cooldown", "add a shop command to my Rust plugin", "what mods do I have for Valheim", "update the boss mod for the new version". Design `RouteDecision = { intent: create|refine|fix|explain|install|unknown, gameId, categoryId, projectId?, confidence, reason, clarify? }` in `lib/cyrus/route.ts`.
- **Cost-aware design (the owner wants lower API spend without a dumber product):** a deterministic fast path first (game aliases from the registry, "my <name> mod" fuzzy-matched against the user's own projects and mod titles, intent verbs, category keywords), costing zero API calls. Only genuinely ambiguous input may use ONE tiny structured classification call through the existing cheapest-model plumbing, or (better when cheap enough) show a one-tap clarification chip ("Frost Axe v2 or Frost Axe?"). The current selection/hover always wins as context.
- The UI response: the camera glides to the target node (existing `camera.ts`/`forge.ts` machinery), the branch lights up, the preview opens, the dock shows a chip ("Creating a new Minecraft mod in Weapons" / "Refining Frost Axe"). Unknown or unsupported game: say so plainly and offer supported games.
- Unit tests with 60+ varied phrases (typos, other word orders, multi-game ambiguity, "my mod" with 0/1/many matches). Keep it pure and client-safe so it can run in the dock instantly.

**B. Universal preset categories.** One canonical set, identical across all games (examples the owner gave: Environment, Weapons, Performance; design the final ~14 to 16 so they map cleanly onto the NxLabs mod store; read `lib/cyrus-mods/registry.ts`, the store pages and `lib/cyrus/categories.ts`). For each: id, label, one-line blurb, an **SVG icon** (24x24, `currentColor`, consistent stroke; reuse the existing 12 in `components/icons`/`CategoryIcons.tsx` and draw the missing ones), and per-game availability (a game's `GameSupport.categories` once the game agents land; until then a sensible default table). The **auto-sorter** classifies a finished mod into one primary + up to two secondary categories from the prompt, the generated code and the build metadata, deterministic signals first (zero API), with a cheap fallback only when confidence is low. Mod categories on the map become these presets; migrate existing projects (read-only DB access in dev; write a safe migration helper, do not run it on production).

**C. Listing dialog after a mod is built** (and "Edit listing" when clicking an existing mod): title, category (auto-selected, shows "auto-sorted", easy override), icon/logo (upload, or pick a generated/preset glyph, cropped to the rounded shape), brief description (AI draft from the build summary where free, editable, 280 chars). Define `lib/cyrus/listing.ts` NOW and commit it early: `ModListingInput = { title, categoryId, secondaryCategoryIds, iconAssetId|null, description }` plus validators. The **community agent owns storage** (`saveModListing(projectIdOrBuildId, input)` and the NxLabs page); call it through a thin adapter `lib/cyrus/listing-client.ts` that works with a local fallback until their branch is merged. Do not touch the NxLabs page.

## Verify
Pure tests, then the real route on node-2 with screenshots (the dialog; routing from the core with nothing selected; a refine jump), dark + light, 1440 + 390; `devhost tsc` clean.

content.content:
# Cyrus token economy (design, 2026-10-07)

Branch `feature/cyrus-tokens` (worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-cyrustokens`). Code: `lib/cyrus/tokens/*`.
Every number below is an admin Setting (`cyrus_tok_*`, editable at `/admin/cyrus-tokens`); the
values here are the shipped defaults (`lib/cyrus/tokens/config.ts`). Nothing in this file is a
forecast of customer behaviour: the cost figures are measured builds, the rest are rules.

## 0. The data this is built on

| Source | What | Numbers |
|---|---|---|
| `/root/agent-notes/modbuilder-preview/phase0-builds.jsonl` | 10 real builds, Sonnet 5, pre-tuning | avg $0.28, $0.08-$0.47 |
| docs "AI Mod Builder: tuning" eval (28 prompts) | service 0.3, Sonnet 5.5 | avg $0.104 / median $0.097; simple $0.066, standard $0.102, complex $0.189 |
| same eval, Haiku on simple | Haiku 4.5 | $0.118/build (more turns than Sonnet 5.5), 1/8 failed |
| build service records on VM 88001 (138 builds, read-only) | auto-routed + Cyrus tiers | Haiku-only auto builds avg $0.068 (n=7); Sonnet 5.5 auto avg $0.104 (n=28) |
| Cyrus tier builds (same records) | `tier` set | Katara ChunkMirror change $0.159; Saka ChunkMirror fresh $0.676 (443 s, Sonnet 5); Saka others $0.055 / $0.304; Yakko SimpleHeal $0.341 (Opus 5) |
| ChunkMirror pre-tuning (auto, Sonnet) | | $0.217 |
| Anthropic list prices (per MTok in/out) | | Haiku 4.5 $1/$5 · Sonnet 5 and 5.5 $2/$10 · Opus 5 $5/$25 |
| Refusals (adversarial prompts) | | $0.005-$0.028 |

Two findings the owner should know (not changed by this work, see Owner decisions):
- **Saka maps to Sonnet 5, not 5.5** (`MB_TIER_SAKA`). The tuned default routing uses 5.5, which
  was cheaper, faster and more reliable in the eval. The one Saka-tier ChunkMirror cost $0.676,
  3x the auto-routed one.
- **Katara (Haiku 4.5) is not cheaper per build than Sonnet 5.5** on simple mods ($0.118 vs
  $0.061 in the eval), because it takes about twice the turns. The economy still prices tokens
  on the real cost, so this only affects how much a Katara build spends, never the margin.

## 1. What a token is

**1 token = $0.002 of measured AI cost** (`cyrus_tok_tokens_per_usd = 500`), times a per-model
multiplier: Katara x1.0, Saka x1.0, **Yakko x1.25** (Opus runs vary more and hold a build slot
about twice as long). A build that reached the AI costs at least 5 tokens (`cyrus_tok_min_spend`).

    tokens charged = max(5, ceil(costUsd x 500 x multiplier[model]))

`costUsd` is the build service's own number for that build (`ModBuild.costUsd`). The token is a
*cost* unit, so margin lives entirely in what a token *sells* for (section 3), and Yakko costing
many more tokens than Katara falls out of the real costs (Opus is 5x Haiku per token).

### Tokens per typical build

| Model | Typical (measured) | Tokens | Big build | Tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Katara | simple $0.068 (auto Haiku avg) | **34** | ChunkMirror change $0.159 | **80** |
| Saka | $0.104 (Sonnet 5.5 avg) / $0.189 complex | **52** / 95 | Sonnet 5 tier: $0.30 / $0.676 | 150 / 338 |
| Yakko | simple $0.341 (measured) | **214** | complex ~$1.18 (Opus 2.5x Sonnet 5 complex $0.47, extrapolated) | ~738 |

Pre-build estimate shown in the composer (`cyrus_tok_reserve_table`, tokens, [typical, high]):

| | simple | standard | complex |
|---|---|---|---|
| Katara | 30-70 | 60-140 | 100-240 |
| Saka | 35-100 | 60-220 | 110-400 |
| Yakko | 100-250 | 200-500 | 400-1000 |

Complexity comes from the existing `lib/cyrus/estimate.ts` feature count (unchanged).

## 2. Game-server grants

    per-month amount = clamp(round5(base + perUsd x monthly price $), min, max)
    initial:  base 100, perUsd 16, min 150, max 750
    renewal:  base 25,  perUsd 6,  min 40,  max 300

`monthly price` = what the customer actually paid per month (after coupons/partner discount,
before tax). Prepaid terms: an N-month purchase gets initial + renewal x (N-1); an N-month
renewal gets renewal x N; N capped at 12 (`cyrus_tok_grant_term_months_cap`).

| Monthly price | Initial | AI cost if all used (% of 1st month) | Every renewal | (% of renewal) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $2.99 | 150 | $0.30 (10.0%) | 45 | $0.09 (3.0%) |
| $4.99 | 180 | $0.36 (7.2%) | 55 | $0.11 (2.2%) |
| $8.99 | 245 | $0.49 (5.5%) | 80 | $0.16 (1.8%) |
| $9.99 | **260** | $0.52 (5.2%) | 85 | $0.17 (1.7%) |
| $15.99 | 355 | $0.71 (4.4%) | 120 | $0.24 (1.5%) |
| $30.00 | 580 | $1.16 (3.9%) | 205 | $0.41 (1.4%) |
| $49.99+ | 750 (cap) | $1.50 | 300 (cap) | $0.60 |

($0.159); even the pre-tuning $0.217 ChunkMirror is 109 tokens. Either way more than half is left

I'm weighing whether to build this demo as plain JS in page.js or as a React component, since the core relies on createCoreGL from the TS cosmos modules. Since that needs bundling, I'll create a hand-written React client component, CyrusDemo, under app/nxm/cyrus/, with a layout mounting a CyrusDemoMount wrapper so the whole thing can stay in TS/React.

The layout should mount quietly even if the page 404s, finding no slot and rendering nothing without leaking content. For the demo component itself, I'm sketching its structure: reading game, category, model, and reserve data from a JSON blob in the DOM, then rendering a stage area with a canvas for links and visuals, responsive between desktop and mobile aspect ratios.

Questions about bare metal dedicated servers

The things people ask before ordering.

What is a bare metal dedicated server?

A physical server reserved entirely for you. There is no virtualisation layer between you and the hardware and no other customer on it, so all of its CPU, memory, disks and network port are yours.

What do the NX names mean?

The class plus the size. NX-Core is proven entry hardware, NX-Pulse is high-clock desktop CPUs, NX-Forge is current server CPUs, NX-Titan is many-core and dual-socket, NX-GPU has a dedicated GPU. The numbers are total cores and memory in GB, so NX-Forge 8-64 has 8 cores and 64 GB. The exact CPU model is on every build.

How fast is setup?

You can only order builds that are in stock, and they are online within 24 hours of your order. The server page shows each step while our team works through it.

Can I reinstall or reboot it myself?

Yes. From the server page you can hard reboot, boot into a rescue system using your SSH key, and wipe and reinstall a fresh operating system. A remote console is available through our team.

Which operating systems can I install?

Current Ubuntu LTS, Debian, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux and Proxmox VE releases supported by your build. You log in as root with your own SSH key.

How does billing work?

Pay monthly, or a year up front. The renewal is stated exactly as it will be charged, and any one-time setup fee is shown on the build before you pay. Pay by card, from your wallet, or both.

Can I get more IP addresses?

Yes. Add a single extra IPv4 or a small block from the server page. Our team confirms availability in your location before it is added, and you are refunded in full if it can't be.

Can I order hardware that is not listed?

No. Every build we sell is on this page, in stock, and priced. The list changes through the day as machines are reserved and freed up.

One account for everything

Bare metal, next to the rest of your stack.

Your dedicated servers live in the same dashboard, wallet and support queue as your VPS, game servers, domains and email. Move a workload up when it outgrows a VPS, without changing how you work.

What is Cyrus?

Cyrus is Nxeon's AI mod studio. You describe a game mod in plain words and it plans the mod, writes the code, compiles it, checks it for safety and installs it on your server. It runs in your Nxeon dashboard.

Which games does it support?

Today Cyrus builds real, compiled server plugins for {{nxm:liveNames}}, on Paper and Purpur {{nxm:versions}}. Palworld, Rust, Valheim, Project Zomboid and Terraria are on the map and in development: the studio can draft mods for them as a template preview, but they are not compiled or installable yet.

Do my players need to install anything?

Not for Minecraft. Cyrus makes Paper plugins, which run on the server only, so players join with the normal game. Some other games need a file on every player's computer too; Cyrus will say so plainly for each game before you build.

Is the code safe to run on my server?

Every build is compiled and then scanned before you see it. Code that connects to the internet, runs other programs on the machine, loads code at runtime or can shut the server down is blocked. Anything sensitive, such as changing operators or running console commands, is flagged so you can decide.

What are tokens?

Tokens pay for the AI work a build does. Each build is charged for what it really used, never a flat fee, and the studio shows an estimate before you start. Tokens come with every paid Minecraft server, with a monthly plan, or as a top-up.

What is the difference between Katara, Saka and Yakko?

They are Cyrus's three models. Katara is fast and spends the fewest tokens, good for simple mods and small tweaks. Saka is the balanced builder for most mods. Yakko reasons longest for big systems like bosses and quest lines, and spends the most.

Do I own the mods I make?

Yes. You can download the plugin file and the full source for every version. Your mod page stays private until you choose to publish it.

What happens if a build fails?

Cyrus tries to fix compile errors itself before giving up. If a build still fails because of a problem on our side, your first {{nxm:freeFailures}} failures in {{nxm:freeFailuresDays}} days cost nothing.

How it works

From one sentence to a mod on your server

Eight steps, each one a real part of the product. Where a step is still being built, it says so.

  1. 01

    Describe it

    Live

    Write what the mod should do, the way you would tell a friend. Commands, numbers, who can use it. Cyrus estimates the work before it starts and recommends a model, so a small tweak never runs on the most expensive one.

    A frost greatsword that slows enemies on critical hits and leaves a short ice trail. Operators get it with /frostblade give <player>.
    {{nxm:icon:saka}}SakaPaper {{nxm:mcVersion}}Estimate: {{nxm:est}} tokens↵
  2. 02

    Cyrus routes it

    Live

    Every request runs through the core and down the right branch: the game, then the category, then your mod. You can start from the core, a game or a mod you already have. Understanding broad requests like "work on my frost axe and fix the cooldown" from anywhere is being added now.

    CoreMinecraftWeaponsFrost greatsword

    Creating a new Minecraft mod in Weapons

  3. 03

    Forge and verify

    Live

    Cyrus plans the files, writes them, and compiles them against the real server API for the version you picked. If the compiler complains, it reads the error and fixes the code itself. Then a safety scan reads the compiled code: anything that reaches the internet, runs programs on the machine or shuts the server down is blocked, not just flagged.

      {{nxm:stages:html}}
  4. 04

    Read it, test it, refine it

    Live

    Every file is yours to read, with notes and an explanation of what the mod does. Install it on a server, try it in game, then ask for changes in plain words. Each change is a new version, and you can go back to any of them.

version: 1.0.0
main: dev.cyrus.frostbite.FrostbiteBladePlugin
api-version: '1.21'
commands:

    usage: /frostblade give <player>
permissions:
  frostblade.give:
    default: op
    • v2 Add a short ice trail behind the player
    • v1 First build

  5. 05

    Put it on NxLabs

    Live

    Every finished mod gets its own page on NxLabs, the Nxeon mod store. It stays private until you publish it. Give it a title, a category, an icon and a short description, and it carries the Built with Cyrus badge.

    Let the community build on it

    Partly live

    Anyone can press Build on this mod and start their own copy in their Cyrus, with yours credited as the original. Players post notes, bug reports and fixes on the page. Next: remixes listed as community versions under the original, and loading any community mod straight into your Cyrus.

  7. 07

    Install it on your server

    Live

    Pick one of your Minecraft servers and press install. Nxeon takes a backup of the plugins folder, writes the new file next to the old one, swaps it in and keeps the old copy for a rollback. The mod then shows up in the server's Mods tab like any other plugin.

  8. 08

    Updates and warnings

    Partly live

    When you make a new version, the server's Mods tab shows that an update is available. Switch a mod off and on, update it, roll it back or remove it without touching files. Next: a warning when a game update may break a mod, and a heads-up to its creator.

One studio, {{nxm:gameCount}} games, each with its own modding rules

Every game loads mods differently: a different language, a different loader, and sometimes a file every player has to install too. Cyrus learns each one properly before it builds for it, so a mod never breaks a server it was not made for.

    {{nxm:games:html}}

Models and plans

Three minds, priced by what a build really uses

Katara is quick, Saka is the balanced builder, Yakko thinks longest. Cyrus charges tokens for the work a build actually does, so a small mod costs little and a big system costs more.

    {{nxm:models:html}}
    {{nxm:plans:html}}

Mods that people build on

A Cyrus mod is a starting point. Publish yours and other people can take it further, credited back to you, with their changes kept alongside the original.

Same preview gate (`requireModBuilderUser()` on every page, `modBuilderUser()` on every API). The portal sidebar and top bar stay; the studio fills the app frame.

**Where it lives.** UI `components/cyrus/{chrome,cosmos,cores,icons,preview,prompt}` + `CyrusApp.tsx` (handoff components, imports re-rooted); state/engine `lib/cyrus/{store,forge,fx,data,types,camera,hooks,zip,highlight}.ts` + `lib/cyrus/engine/` (template generators); game logos `public/cyrus/games/`. Kept from v4: `components/cyrus/kit/` (icon set used by the token modal, the install-to-server modal), `lib/cyrus/{projects,meta,models,estimate,uploads,diff,tokens/}`.

**Scoping (nothing leaks into the portal).** `app/dashboard/cyrus/layout.tsx` wraps every Cyrus route in `.cyrus-root.nx-dark-island` and loads Inter / Space Grotesk / JetBrains Mono as CSS variables on that box only. `studio.css` (handoff globals + network CSS) and `cores/cores.css` are generated from the handoff with every selector under `.cyrus-root`, keyframes and `@property` renamed `cy5-*`, and the three class names that collide with portal globals renamed (`cy5-glass`, `cy5-btn-ghost`, `cy5-kbd`). The root uses `container-type: size; contain: layout paint`, so the handoff's `position: fixed` chrome is contained in the content area; `100vw/vh` became `cqw/cqh`. Tailwind colour tokens are `cy-*` (`text-cy-ink`, `border-cy-line` …, `@theme inline` in `app/globals.css` pointing at variables that exist only on `.cyrus-root`), plus a `cy-light:` variant. `nx-dark-island` keeps the portal's generated light-mode retargeting off the studio (it has its own light theme). `test/cyrus.test.ts` fails if a studio selector is unscoped or a keyframe isn't `cy5-`.

**Theme.** The portal's: `html[data-theme="light"]` / localStorage `nx-theme`. The studio's toggle presses the portal's own toggle button; `useCyrusBoot` mirrors `data-theme` into the store for the canvas and shaders. No `cyrus-theme` key.

**Real vs template.** Minecraft is the one real game (`GAMES[].real`). The account's builds are its Minecraft mods (`lib/cyrus/real.ts deriveReal`: one mod per project, builds = versions, category from the build's own words, at most two extra category branches). Minecraft seeds are dashed **ideas**: clicking one writes a buildable prompt. Notes / restore / favourite are the existing `PATCH /api/mod-builder/projects/:root`; files load lazily from `/api/mod-builder/builds/:id/source`; downloads are the real `.jar` / source zip; **Deploy** opens the v4 install modal. Every other game (and added games) is the handoff's template generator, labelled "Template preview", spends no tokens, kept in localStorage per account (`cyrus-state-v1:<userId>`).

**Forge stream** (`POST /api/cyrus/generate`, NDJSON, handoff §6 GenEvents). A prompt that routes to Minecraft, or a change to a real mod, goes through `lib/modbuilder/create.ts createModBuild` (extracted from `POST /api/mod-builder/builds`, which now calls it too: same validation, rate limits, 2-in-flight cap and token gate); token errors answer JSON 402/403/429 before the stream so `cyrusTokens.handleBuildError` opens the modal. Then `lib/cyrus/follow.ts` streams the real build: stage changes → `think`, the service `/live` draft → `file`/`chunk`, in-place edits → `file-set`, keep-alive `ping`, final source + `done {tokens: charged}` or `error`. `GET ?follow=<id>` re-attaches (page load with a running build, dropped connection; the client retries 4×). Template games run the handoff's `forgeStream()` (no model call). Additive event types: `build`, `file-set`, `ping`.

**Tokens** (UI-CONTRACT.md): `<CyrusTokensHost/>` in `CyrusApp`; `<CyrusTokenChip compact/>` replaces the handoff's credit counter in the top bar; `<CyrusTokenEstimate/>` in the prompt dock for real targets; `<CyrusModelLock/>` + typical token range per model + `<CyrusModelPanelFoot/>` in the model picker; `cyrusTokens.refresh()` after each real build. **Verification** (node-2, devhost): throwaway DB seeded by `.cyrus-verify/seed.ts` (not committed), a local stand-in of the build service (`.cyrus-verify/mock-svc.mjs`, same HTTP as the VM; the portal's real create/sync/live/source/jar code runs unchanged), Playwright screenshots in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-redesign/shots/`.

### Cyrus token economy (2026-10-07, branch `feature/cyrus-tokens`)

Customers pay for Cyrus's AI in **Cyrus tokens**. Design and every number with its reasoning: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-economy/ECONOMY.md`. **Preview-only until launch:** Setting `cyrus_tok_live=false` means only private-preview accounts (`lib/preview-access.ts` "modbuilder") earn grants, see the checkout line, the balance or the plans. Everyone else sees and earns nothing (`lib/cyrus/tokens/access.ts tokensActiveFor`, fails closed). Cyrus is labelled **Beta · Minecraft Java only** wherever tokens appear.

**Unit.** 1 token = $0.002 of the build service's measured `costUsd` (`cyrus_tok_tokens_per_usd=500`), times a model multiplier (Katara 1, Saka 1, Yakko 1.25), min 5 per build that reached the AI. Typical builds: Katara ~34 tokens (ChunkMirror 80), Saka ~52 (complex ~95; Sonnet-5 tier builds 150-338), Yakko ~214 simple. Customers never see a USD figure per token or a model family name (`test/cyrus-tokens-economy.test.ts`).

**Where tokens come from.**
- **Game servers**: on purchase `clamp(round5(100 + 16 x monthly $), 150, 750)`, on every paid renewal `clamp(round5(25 + 6 x monthly $), 40, 300)`; monthly $ = what was actually paid per month. Prepaid N-month terms earn per month (cap 12). Lots expire after 90 days (or term + 30 d). $0 trial starts earn the initial grant on the first paid renewal. Idempotent `gs:<serverId>:initial` / `gs:<serverId>:renew:<periodStartISO>`. Abuse caps: 3 initial grants per account per 30 days, 3,000 unexpired server tokens held. **Only games Cyrus builds for earn** (and get the checkout line): the server's game family must be a `status: "live"` game in `lib/cyrus/games.ts` (`lib/cyrus/tokens/games.ts earnsCyrusTokens`), today Minecraft Java only (`minecraft`; `bedrock` and other games earn nothing). Making a game live there makes its servers earn. `lib/cyrus/games.ts` on this branch is a byte-identical copy of the file on `feature/cyrus-modbuilder` (commit c19b512f86), so the two merge cleanly; if that file changes before the merge, take the modbuilder version. Hooks: `lib/game-order.ts placeGameOrder` (post-commit, `safeGrantPurchase`), `worker/billing.ts commitRenewal` (the single "renewed" exit, every sweep/card/PayPal/admin path) and `lib/actions.ts renewNow` (`safeGrantRenewal`). Never throws into an order or renewal.
- **Plans** (Stripe Billing subscriptions, monthly): Katara $4.99 = 750 tokens/month (Katara), Saka $19.99 = 3,500 (Katara, Saka), All models $49.99 = 10,000 (all three). Every paid invoice grants (`plan:<invoiceId>`), so renewals stack; each month's plan tokens last 3 months from their grant (`cyrus_tok_plan_rollover_months`), so at most 3 months stack. (A first design trimmed to "3 x the current plan" on each invoice; a real test-mode run showed a replayed old invoice could then expire paid tokens, so the cap is by age.) Upgrade = immediate proration (`always_invoice`, tokens in proportion to the money collected); downgrade = at the next renewal; cancel = at period end, plan tokens stay 30 days (Katara only) then expire; past_due keeps the unlock 3 days. Refunds (`charge.refunded`) take back that purchase's unspent tokens pro rata.
- **Top-ups**: one-off Checkout payment, $5-$100, 120 tokens/$, 12-month expiry, no unlock (`topup:<sessionId>`).
- **Admin**: grant / revoke / comp a tier at `/admin/cyrus-tokens`.

**Models.** No plan = Katara only; Katara plan = Katara; Saka plan = Katara + Saka; All models = all three; admin comp can raise it. Enforced server-side in `POST /api/mod-builder/builds` (403 `model_locked`).

  - `__NXM` page data also carries every card, including its `art` (`buildArt()`), its class `tint` (same `FAMILY_TINT` as the portal) and the icon paths (`lib/nx/icon-paths.ts`).
- **GPU band** (mirrors `components/dedicated/flow/GpuBand.tsx`):
  - It is always shown, even with no GPU build in the catalogue.
  - Content: the five GPU renders (`GPU_TIERS`, labels `GPU_TIER_LABEL`), each with "from $X" or "Sold out".
  - In stock: a "See N GPU builds" button filters the catalogue to NX-GPU.

The render box is `min(42%, 190px)` and the title block stops at `right: 45%`, so the name never touches the render, even for the full-width Ultra/GPU renders. The `aurora-veil` plate is bottom-anchored at 118% so the speck at its top edge is cropped.
